title: Addressing Teachers' Stress Levels and Supporting Their Mental Well-being
what_it_is: Addressing Teachers' Stress Levels and Supporting Their Mental Well-being

sections.label: Questions on teacher age and workload
sections.summary: Questions ask whether the low proportion of younger teachers is intended policy, how beginning teachers are supported, and whether non-instructional duties can be reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education given the OECD Teaching and Learning International Survey 2024 finding that only 12% of teachers are aged under 30, with 40% of this group intending to leave within the next five years (a) whether the low proportion of younger teachers is an intended policy outcome; and (b) how are beginning teachers supported to manage the increasing demands of this noble profession.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry is taking any specific steps to further reduce non-instructional duties for teachers, especially marking and administrative work; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider employing full-time employees to assist teachers in communications and event management, amongst other duties, in order to allow teachers to focus on teaching and coaching our children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in light of the findings by the OECD Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2024 dated 7 October 2025 about the increasing complexity of the teaching profession, what are the specific aspects of the teaching profession in Singapore identified by the Ministry with potential for immediate improvement, especially for teachers' welfare.

sections.label: TALIS 2024 working hours finding
sections.summary: The OECD-run TALIS 2024 found Singapore teachers reported longer weekly working hours than the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The 2024 Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS), which is a study run independently by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), found that Singapore teachers reported longer working hours per week compared to the OECD average.

sections.label: Teacher workload stable at 53 hours
sections.summary: Data shows teacher workload has remained stable over the years, averaging 53 total hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As we had said in a written Parliamentary Question reply to this House on 14 October this year, our data shows that, over the years, teacher workload has remained stable in terms of total hours, at an average of 53 hours.

sections.label: AI tools in Student Learning Space
sections.summary: AI and other tech tools in the Singapore Student Learning Space support teachers to plan lessons, mark, give feedback and analyse responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: New AI and other tech tools in the Singapore Student Learning Space (SLS) for example, support teachers to plan lessons, as well as to mark, provide customised feedback and analyse students' responses.

sections.label: Increase in allied educators and admin staff
sections.summary: Over 10 years, allied educators doubled from about 800 to 1,600 and administrative staff rose from six to around nine per school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, we have doubled the number of allied educators across all schools, from about 800 to 1,600, and also increased the number of administrative staff in each school, from six then, to around nine today.

sections.label: Holiday protected time and communication guidelines
sections.summary: Teachers get six to seven weeks protected time across four holiday blocks, and refreshed guidelines avoid parent-staff communication after school hours except emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Across the four blocks of school holidays, teachers can get around six to seven weeks of protected time and can take their vacation leave beyond the protected time, if they do not have any work in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MOE also refreshed the School-Home Partnership guidelines at the end of 2024 to avoid parent-staff communication after school hours, except for critical emergencies.

sections.label: Teacher resignation rates and TALIS
sections.summary: Teacher resignation rates stayed around 2% to 3% over decades, and TALIS 2024 found many teachers felt valued and saw teaching as attractive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The mean annual resignation rates of teachers have remained stable at around 2% to 3% over the past few decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: TALIS 2024 also found that many of our teachers felt valued by society and see teaching as an attractive career choice.

sections.label: Workload audits and non-teaching load
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry conducted recent workload audits to pinpoint pressure sources and reduce the non-teaching bulk.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Has the Ministry conducted any recent workload audits, so that we can pinpoint exactly where this pressure of workload really comes from?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: They have mentioned that the bulk is the non-teaching part, so can we work on something to maybe reduce that further?

sections.label: Fixed guideline to protect teaching time
sections.summary: The question asks whether a white space could be explored to set a fixed guideline across schools protecting core teaching time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Going forward, can we explore a white space, where we put a fixed guideline throughout the different schools to protect core teaching time.

sections.label: More support for some schools
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry would consider giving some schools a lot more support in this regard.

sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider giving some schools a lot more support in this regard?

sections.label: Internal reviews and teacher recruitment
sections.summary: The Ministry says it holds regular internal reviews including teacher workload, and announced in July it will ramp up teacher recruitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have our own internal reviews on a regular basis on a whole variety of issues, including teacher workload, and the various measures that were outlined earlier – and I would not repeat all of them – are in reality, a response to the identified areas of workload which we can moderate or adjust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, some of it involves hiring more and we have announced in July this year that we are going to ramp up the recruitment of teachers.

sections.label: Teacher hours versus other workers
sections.summary: TALIS notes teachers average 47 hours a week, unchanged over the last decade, while Singapore full-time workers' average hours fell from about 47 to 44.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: Because it is very concerning when TALIS, not just notes that teachers on average work 47 hours a week, but that the number has not gone down over the last two seasons of the survey over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: Whereas across Singapore, for full-time workers, the average hours worked went down from about 47 hours to about 44 hours.

sections.label: Beginning teachers intending to leave
sections.summary: The survey noted a low proportion of beginning teachers and that many intended to leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: For beginning teachers, the survey noted that the proportion of teachers was low and that many were intending to leave.

sections.label: Teacher recruitment reduced then ramped up
sections.summary: Recruitment was reduced to 650 to 700 teachers a year from 2018 to 2024, and in July it was announced it would ramp up to 1,000 or more per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Well, in 2018 to 2024, with falling cohorts and a maturing workforce, we had reduced recruitment to some 650 to 700 teachers a year, in order to fill in the gaps in certain subjects and to replace retiring teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But in July this year, we announced that we will ramp up recruitment of teachers going forward to some 1,000 teachers or more per year.

sections.label: Support for beginning teachers' attrition
sections.summary: Beginning teachers are supported through inductions, mentoring, supportive school cultures, professional development, and flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To the Member's second question about beginning teachers' attrition, we support them through inductions, through mentoring in the first few years, through more supportive environments in school culture, focusing on professional development to enable our beginning teachers to be able to navigate, what will inevitably be a steep learning curve in teaching and in fact, in all professions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also need to accommodate, adjust and respond to a changing demographic with different aspirations of work and life, and so, in that regard, having more flexible work arrangements, including part-time teaching, having various options for teachers to adjust their school day, specific to their own responsibilities and specific to the school environment.

sections.label: Appraisal, teacher surveys and parent engagement
sections.summary: Appraisal considers teachers' holistic work and performance, and surveys and engagement with teachers and unions inform changes such as Parents Gateway and MOE's Engagement Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In response to her first question on appraisal, we do take into account the teachers' holistic work as well as performance – teaching, CCAs, projects and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of whether we do surveys of teachers or engage teachers to better understand the relationship between them and parents, the answer is yes – through dialogues, through feedback from STU and other teachers' unions, through our well-being surveys, we get a better understanding of the changing demographic of parents today and their expectations of their children and teachers in school and out of school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Hence, as a result, you see changes such as the Parents Gateway, implemented a number of years ago, School-Home Partnership as well as MOE's Engagement Charter, which sets out clearer boundaries and expectations, and draws clearer lines between teachers and parents – so that we can have a good productive, holistic relationship and partnership for the benefit of our children.

sections.label: Teacher workload and education reforms
sections.summary: Working hours are long and require collective effort, and there have been a series of education reforms and changes over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of the workload, I mentioned in response to another Member earlier that the stability of our working hours – not that we crow about it; certainly, those are long hours and we need to continue to work collectively at it and I think, on both sides of this House, we all recognise and appreciate our teachers putting in all this effort for the benefit of holistic education of our children – but there has been a whole series of education reforms and changes over the years.

sections.label: Safeguards for accurate MOE surveys
sections.summary: MOE surveys have a high response rate and include clear guidelines, instructions and worked examples to capture accurate workload data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member's first question is about safeguards to ensure that our MOE surveys capture accurate data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have a large teaching workforce – primary, secondary, junior college, centralised institute – and the surveys have a very high response rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Something like more than 90% of our teachers respond because they know that if they give us accurate information, it will enable our policy-makers to better roll out measures that support them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And so, to help do this, in our surveys, we have clear guidelines and instructions on how to itemise the workload for different kinds of work, both in classroom and outside classroom, pedagogical as well as administrative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also provide worked examples that enable our teachers, particularly those who are doing surveys for the first time, to better understand what we are trying to capture.
